holidays.name: No Dirty Dishes Day
holidays.description: A day to give your sink a break. Use paper plates, order takeout, or eat straight from the pot, and leave no pile of dishes behind. Your hands stay dry and your sponge gets the day off.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a favorite on fun-holiday calendars, and the people who keep it are mostly grateful for the break.
holidays.funFact: Dishwashing is one of the most disliked household chores. That may be why a holiday about skipping it caught on.

holidays.name: National Cheese Soufflé Day
holidays.description: A salute to the puffy, golden, cheesy dish that has a reputation for collapsing the moment you open the oven door. Bakers are invited to whisk, fold, and hope.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It honors a classic of French cooking.
holidays.funFact: The word soufflé comes from the French verb meaning to blow or puff up. The dish gets its lift from egg whites beaten into a foam.

holidays.name: Plant a Lemon Tree Day
holidays.description: A day for gardeners to plant a lemon tree, whether in a backyard or in a pot on a sunny windowsill. When life gives you lemons, you can say you grew them yourself.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial gardening observance of unclear origin. It is a sunny nudge to get something citrusy into the soil.
holidays.funFact: Some lemon varieties, such as the Meyer lemon, grow well in containers. That means you can have a lemon tree even without a yard.
